summary: Independent five-lens review of the S1 suite statistics spike (proof, re-implementation, simulation, claims, product contract), then adversarial verification of each finding

sound.checked_and_sound: The validity argument holds; I found no error that touches the guarantee. (1) For any delta in (0,1) and q in [0,1] the factors are at least 1-q >= 0 and have conditional expectation 1 +/- lambda(E[d|past]+delta) <= 1 under the respective null (exact check over six deltas by five q values, equality at the boundary). (2) decide() (suite_stats.py:140-146) and count_wealth() (164-176) average products with fixed equal weights, not stakes, so each wealth is a nonnegative supermartingale started at 1. (3) Ville with inclusive >= is the correct side, classify()'s integer test is exactly W >= 2/alpha, and checkpoints, first-stop and the cap only shrink the crossing event; the spike's exact DP at alpha=1/5, delta=1/4, batch 1, cap 60 gives boundary maxima 0.058 PASS and 0.050 BLOCK against a limit of 0.1. (4) Uniform with-replacement draws independent of the past give E[d_i|past]=Delta whatever the cell heterogeneity or within-pair dependence; what breaks otherwise is the per-step conditional mean: a fixed-order cycle with 70 tied cells first and 230 always-regressing cells after (suite mean -23/30) returns PASS at pair 70 from decide(), while for fixed stakes a complete balanced block still has product expectation <= 1 by AM-GM, so only mid-block looks are unprotected (my derivation, not in the spike). (5) Simultaneous crossing is impossible for any fixed or mixture rule because (1+ax)^b (1-bx)^a <= 1 pathwise, so one component >= c > 1 forces every opposite component below 1; confirmed by zero ERROR frontier states for n=10..400 and zero ERROR mass in all 120 Table A rows (full-support batch-1 rows to n=1000), and ERROR lies inside both crossing events so it cannot inflate either error (the adaptive rule can reach it: single look on sixty +1 then two hundred -1 gives ERROR). (6) The pathwise monotone coupling is correct for fixed p_zero (first PASS-crossing time falls, first BLOCK-crossing time rises, so PASS implies PASS' and BLOCK' implies BLOCK); error control does not depend on it, only the reading of Table A does. (7) An independent float DP reproduced four Table A cells to eight decimals (cap 400 batch 10 at p_zero 11/20: 0.01045702 / 0.00979489; at 2/5: 0.01028935 / 0.01017187; cap 400 batch 20 at 9/10: 0.00821431; cap 100 batch 1 at 1/5: 0.01241542 / 0.01160767), and the integer frontier matched count_wealth plus classify on 1,976 edge states at the defaults with 0 mismatches. That last check is one the spike's own tests make only at alpha=1/2, delta=1/3, n <= 25, and Tables A, B and the five agreement points all share that frontier rather than calling decide(), so the product should carry a default-parameter frontier-versus-reference test.

No bug or validity gap found in the reference procedure, the enumeration or Table A. My own Fraction implementation agreed with suite_stats.decide on all 2,539,107 ordered paths tried (max_pairs 8-12, batch 1/2/3/5, alpha 1/2, 1/5, 1/20) in verdict, stopping pair and every checkpoint wealth, including terminal partial batches and decisions exactly at the cap. Brute-force path probabilities matched suite_stats_sim.characteristics as exact Fractions in 1,088 of 1,088 comparisons (34 plans x 8 trinomials, including zero-probability categories and max_pairs < batch), and again for rules with q=1 where wealth sticks at zero. An independent absorbing recursion that evaluates every state directly, with no monotone-frontier assumption, equalled results.json exactly for 360 Table A entries: cap 50 batch 10 boundary-PASS max 0.00466184 at p_zero 1/5, cap 100 batch 20 0.00454541 at 3/5, default cap 400 batch 10 0.01045702 with null BLOCK 0.01017187, and the headline 0.02090523 (cap 1000, batch 1, p_zero 0). The frontiers were monotone at every look from 10 to 400, and a p_zero grid of step 1/400 at cap 400 moved the maxima only in the fifth or sixth decimal (0.01046262 against 0.01045702), so the 1/20 grid is representative. Table C's Monte Carlo for fixed and mixture rules is consistent with my exact values (mixture 0.80->0.80 cap 400: exact 0.74337 against 0.74850; fixed 0.57417 against 0.57345), the earlier run log's tables are byte-identical to the current RESULTS.md, and the source hashes in results.json match the files on disk. decide() edge behaviour is as documented: short or empty streams raise, bool and float inputs are rejected, max_pairs < batch gives one look at the cap, a suffix after the decisive checkpoint is ignored, and a 4,000-pair inconclusive stream decides in 0.9 s. The supermartingale algebra, stake caps, the Ville bound and the monotone-coupling argument (including the simultaneous-crossing case) hold as written, and Table D's v1 figures match docs/STATISTICS.md.

All checks were run read-only in memory against results.json, whose source hashes match the current .py files; the tables in run-full.log and RESULTS.md are identical (only the elapsed time differs, 292.9 s in CODEX_REPORT.md versus 537.3 s in RESULTS.md, a rerun). Table B construction is sound: all 72 scenarios have suite mean exactly -1/10 (asserted at suite_stats_sim.py:285 and re-verified), cells are drawn uniformly with replacement before and independently of the outcome draw, the joint categorical draw reproduces the marginals and couplings, and the 72 B seeds, 90 C seeds and 5 agreement seeds are unique and disjoint. Clopper-Pearson: my independent lgamma/bisection inversion gives 0.0123555, 0.0062321, 0.0133246, 0.0078385 for k = 211, 99, 229, 128 at n = 20000 versus the spike's 0.0123558, 0.0062323, 0.0133247, 0.0078392 (all within the stated 2^-20 upward rounding), and 16 further bounds matched; the B maximum is 0.013755. Table A: my own float DP reproduces the exact entries to about 1e-13, and the integer frontiers match classify(count_wealth) on every state for n = 10, 20, 30, 50; on a p_zero grid of step 0.01 refined to 0.001 at cap 400, batch 10, the boundary PASS maximum is 0.01046263 at p_zero 0.568 (spike grid: 0.01045702 at 0.55) and the BLOCK maximum 0.01017478 at 0.412 (spike: 0.01017187 at 0.40), so the 0.05 grid is adequate; I did not refine the cap 1000, batch 1 row (2.09 percent). Table C: scenarios are built as stated, mean pairs includes capped runs (stops[n] at n = max_pairs), and all 30 mixture rows agree with exact DP (max |z| 2.16, sum z^2 47.4 over 72 non-degenerate terms). The float fast path decides Tables C and D only (B uses integer frontiers): it matched the integer frontier on 4,500 random 400-pair streams and 4,778 frontier-adjacent single-look streams for mixture and fixed, and the exact rational decide on 120 adaptive streams, with zero mismatches; the closest exact wealth to the threshold was 1.6e-4 relative, far outside the 1e-10 fallback band.

Every number quoted in CODEX_REPORT.md and the RESULTS.md decision section matches results.json: Table A maximum 0.020905 (batch 1, cap 1000, boundary BLOCK, p_zero 0) with zero of 120 rows above 1/40 by exact integer comparison, and 0.010457 at the recommended batch 10 / cap 400; Table B maximum 99% bound 0.013755 over 72 points; mixture/adaptive ratio 0.6236 to 1.1667 with 23 of 30 at or below 1; 29 tests; 351 golden vectors; all Table D v2 costs equal twice the Table C capped means. RESULTS.md was regenerated by the second run and its table rows are byte-identical to run-full.log, so the seeded results reproduce; only the elapsed time differs. An independent float absorbing-state DP over the spike's own integer frontiers reproduces Table C for the fixed and mixture rules within Monte Carlo error (for example 0.95/0.95 cap 200 PASS .906 vs .9029, 0.95->0.75 cap 400 BLOCK .9036 vs .9029). The published v1 inputs in Table D match docs/STATISTICS.md and my rerun of bench/selfcheck.py functions (.889, .9895, .365, .838, .985, .9998, .218, .706; sequential .735 at 350, .969 at 239, .943 at 302, .9989 at 159). The supermartingale algebra and stake caps in CONTRACT.md are correct, and the spike is candid that the 15% criterion against adaptive failed, that expected pairs are capped stopping times, and that strong-positive v2 cases are not compared with independent v1 numbers. The equal mixture with batch 10 and cap 400 is a sound recommendation for error control and a reasonable robustness compromise; my findings concern what is claimed about it, not its validity. I did not run suite_stats_sim.py as a script, wrote no files, and did not re-run pytest.

The signs, stake caps and fixed-mixture construction in suite_stats.py match CONTRACT.md. The exact boundary value for (1/10, 9/10, 0) is P(PASS) = 0.974%, and my independent SHA-256 schedule gave 29 PASS in 3000 manifests; my IID cell simulation at batch=20 gave 0.75-0.82% false PASS and 0.74-0.81% false BLOCK against Table A's 0.82% and 0.80%. A simultaneous PASS and BLOCK crossing is unreachable for the default mixture at every n up to 400 and every multiple of 10 up to 1000 (the smallest gap between the two frontiers is 31 counts), so the ERROR branch in classify is a dead invariant for the defaults. The requirement that an errored or missing pair is ERROR, never dropped or scored 0, is necessary for validity, since dropping conditions the sample on an event the candidate can influence. For parallel execution the v1 pattern carries over with stage = batch: runner.py:1568-1593 submits one stage, waits for all of it, stores, then decides, so no pair beyond the next checkpoint is ever started and nothing is in flight at a stop. If speculation past a checkpoint is added later, those results must be cancelled or discarded and never stored. The v2 gate must mirror gate.py:328-370: recompute the schedule, require the stored pairs to be exactly indices 0 to n_stop-1 with both arms, order by schedule index and not completion order, and require every earlier checkpoint INCONCLUSIVE and the last one decisive or equal to max_pairs. It cannot delegate this to the reference, which ignores a padded suffix (decide([0]*70+[-1]*330) returns PASS at 70; suite_stats.py:133,149-150); mixture wealth depends only on counts, so completion order within a batch cannot change a verdict. Beyond the findings, the ASSUMED lines that are cheap to enforce are the freeze of grid, rule, stakes, batch and cap (bound through spec_sha256 and a digest-derived seed), a required non-empty and verified fixtures_sha256 (schema.py:398 defaults to ''), and the prefix rule above; stationarity, cross-pair independence and provider drift stay undetected, as CONTRACT.md says.

**Nit, not enough to change the verdict.** The exact limit is 0.0082143064, which displays as 0.00821431; read literally, "at least 0.00821431" overstates what this evidence shows by about 4e-9. No tolerant option, pair-level re-draw rule or resume rule appears in CONTRACT.md, RESULTS.md, CODEX_REPORT.md or PLAN.md section 2 (grepped for retr/resum/imput/void).
- **The agent can trigger ERROR.** `docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md` lines 256-260 and `src/arci/runner.py` lines 1356-1360 make a command agent's exit code in `infra_exit_codes` (default 75) a `HARNESS_ERROR`. Line 77 of the semantics doc and `runner.py` lines 635-636 make an invalid or wrong-nonce frame an error.
- **Void on any ERROR.** `src/arci/gate.py` lines 320-324 add the global reason "trial outcome ERROR". `src/arci/storage.py` lines 13-14 raise `FileExistsError` on a non-empty run directory, and there is no retry or resume code in `src/arci`.
- **Void arithmetic.** 1-(1-e)^s gives 0.2087 and 0.5509 at e=0.1% for 234 and 800 sessions, and 0.6905 and 0.9819 at e=0.5%. RESULTS.md line 164 gives a mean of 117.33 pairs for the mixture at cap 400, which is the 234 sessions.
- **Imputation algebra.** In exact Fractions with the spike's `Plan`, every mixture component's factor is exactly 1-q for d=-1 in W_plus and for d=+1 in W_minus, and that is the minimum over d in {-1,0,+1}. A brute-force check over 300 random streams with random error masks, at every prefix, found imputed wealth never above true wealth in either direction. Since the imputed crossing event is contained in the latent stream's crossing event, Ville's bound carries over under any completion of the errored pairs that satisfies the null.
- **Cost by `count_wealth`.** An all-zero stream first reaches W_plus >= 40 at 70, 80, 100, 120, 150 and 200 pairs with 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 imputed errors, exactly as claimed.
- **Monte Carlo.** My own 20,000-rep run (0.95 vs 0.95 independent, per-session e, float wealth, seed 12345):

| e per session | P(PASS) | Mean pairs | Runs with at least one error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1% | 99.8% | 122.7 | 20.6% |
| 0.5% | 98.98% | 147.9 | 63.6% |
| 2% | 62.1% | 288.1 | 95.9% |

  The reviewer's 62.4% and 286 at e=2% are within Monte Carlo error. As an extra check at the boundary (0.95 vs 0.85) with imputation, false PASS was 0.56% and false BLOCK 0.40% at e=0.5%, both under 2.5%.

**What is overstated**

- **"Will void most long live runs."** This depends on an assumed error rate; no measured harness-error rate is cited. At e=0.1% about 21% of typical runs void. The 55% figure applies only at the 800-session cap, which 0.1% of runs reach in that scenario. "Most" needs roughly e >= 0.3% per session.
- **"Silent on retries" and "a blanket retry is unsafe."** Nobody proposes a retry. The contract and plan already choose void-on-ERROR and already name "retries until green" as breaking the proof. The real gap is narrower: no explicit ban on re-drawing an errored pair, no resume rule, and no tolerant alternative.
- **"No resume."** This is a fact about the v1 store. The v2 suite store is unwritten (PLAN phase 2), so it is an unstated requirement, not a spike defect.
- **Invalid-frame path.** I confirmed exit 75 in code as agent-controlled. I did not confirm that every agent type can reach the invalid-frame path.
- **"Needs no assumption."** The imputation still needs a latent completed stream that satisfies the IID null. It needs no assumption about why the error occurred.
- **Severity.** The recommended default is what the contract already says, so this is an addition to ADR 0011 plus an optional extension, not a forced design change.
